PullRequest.Title: Fixes github pr and issue link presentation data fetching

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering GitHub repository, issue, and pull-request links as rich links in chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A link watcher must obtain a GitHub credential and then subscribe to the corresponding resource before details appear. Repository and issue bulk hydration and pull-request/resource fetches are on this presentation critical path; the new warning/notification handling runs only after an error and does not delay successful rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the current GitHub identity with GET /user when no credential generation is cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared identity request per token/endpoint generation; concurrent watchers reuse the current promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same credential resolution and request coalescing occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks creation of the first resource subscription for a new credential generation; warm generations reuse the resolved credential.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bulk-hydrate repository and issue resources, then subscribe/fetch repository, issue, or pull-request fragments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Repository and issue links created in one microtask are deduplicated and grouped into one hydration request per account; subscriptions are shared per canonical resource, while pull-request core/check fragment work is scheduled per unique pull request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same hydration grouping, resource subscriptions, priorities, and network cardinality existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These GitHub reads provide the presentation data and are on the cold path; shared service/resource caches serve duplicate or warm watchers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit a warning and possibly create one sticky authentication notification when a presentation reaches an error state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One _setPresentation invocation per observable state update per unique active resource; authentication notifications are coalesced to one live handle for the contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Errors updated the presentation without warning logging or an authentication notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after an error, not on the successful data-fetch critical path. Logging cost scales with error-state updates, but the traced update frequency and shared watcher cardinality do not establish a material regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct GitHub URLs currently rendered, after canonical-resource sharing and hydration deduplication; duplicate renderers for the same URL do not add provider watchers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Link presentation entries are shared by provider/resource; repository and issue hydration is microtask-batched, deduplicated, and issued once per account group, while the existing GitHub queues/schedulers govern request concurrency. The notification is explicitly coalesced to one live handle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The data-channel service restores cached presentations and shares active entries; GitHub transport retains ETags and coalesces in-flight REST/GraphQL reads. Cold links fetch data, while warm/duplicate links reuse these layers. The diff does not alter these cache keys or invalidation paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the watcher sharing, hydration grouping, network path, and error callback placement from the traced implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large chats can contain many distinct links, but no evidence shows the added error-only warning work dominates the existing failed network/resource updates; the authentication notification remains bounded to one.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: successful-path boundary count and concurrency are unchanged, and the new error UI is bounded/coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolving a repository-capable GitHub authentication session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getToken waits for authentication-session enumeration and, only when no compatible session is already present, a repo-scoped session lookup/creation. This precedes cold credential and link data fetching.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate GitHub authentication sessions via IAuthenticationService.getSessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One all-session query per getToken call, plus one repo-scoped query only when no compatible repo session for the selected account is already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first session enumeration already occurred, and the old code performed the second repo-scoped query whenever the default session itself lacked repo scope, even if another compatible session existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both calls are awaited before a token can be returned; when an existing compatible session is found, the changed code removes the second awaited query.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of authentication sessions for the provider, normally small; local scans remain linear in that count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: getToken does not add its own fan-out; credential consumers may call it concurrently, while the authentication service controls provider request serialization. The diff reduces conditional query cardinality for an existing compatible session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The GitHub credential service shares the resolved credential generation and identity promise, but token-provider session enumeration occurs when getToken is invoked. The changed compatible-session scan avoids a second query in a newly covered warm-session case.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct getToken implementation and credential-service callers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication-provider implementation cost varies, but the before/after call count is clear and non-regressive.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; this path can avoid an existing extra authentication-service boundary call.

Scenarios.Scenario: Executing GitHub REST, GraphQL, and download requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each transport operation reaches fetch through the existing rate-limit queue and retry/redirect logic. Application ETag revalidation remains on REST reads; fetch cache mode remains no-store.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform GitHub fetches for REST, GraphQL, or downloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: one fetch per attempt plus existing bounded redirects/retries; in-flight REST and GraphQL reads remain coalesced by request key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fetches used cache: no-store and additionally sent Cache-Control: no-store; application ETag caching and request coalescing were otherwise identical.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network fetches remain the request critical path. Removing the Cache-Control request header does not add requests, retries, serialization, or response allocation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct transport requests after in-flight coalescing, with bounded retry and redirect counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing account/rate-limit queues and in-flight maps bound and coalesce requests; the diff changes only request headers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser fetch caching remains disabled by cache: no-store. REST's explicit ETag/body cache remains active and unchanged; GraphQL in-flight coalescing is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all three changed fetch call sites and unchanged queue/cache code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser and proxy treatment of the removed header varies, but there is no mechanism for increased work in the changed implementation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; request cardinality, critical path, and cache lifecycle are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating an extension-host link presentation watcher that no current provider accepts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extension-host-to-main-thread request checks the provider registry and immediately returns an error presentation when no watcher is available. The added warning occurs before sending that existing error result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the create-watcher request from extension host to main thread and return the unavailable presentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing IPC request and response per rejected watcher creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same rejected watcher request returned the same unavailable presentation without the warning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC already existed; the added warning is local diagnostic work on the rejection path and does not introduce another cross-process call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format the rejected resource URI and emit a warning through ILogService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One warning per rejected watcher request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the existing unavailable response, but realistic callers select a matching rule before watcher creation and no hot-path rejection multiplicity is established.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of invalid or raced watcher creation requests, not the number of successfully rendered links.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency or fan-out; each rejected RPC is handled independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in this rejection path; successful data-channel entries are shared elsewhere by canonical resource.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-warning-per-rejection mechanism; low evidence of performance magnitude, so it is not reportable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A misbehaving extension could generate many invalid requests, but that is not established as a realistic normal-product trigger for a material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: User accepts the new GitHub authentication-required notification
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The notification is created after an authentication failure. Only an explicit Sign In action awaits defaultAccountService.signIn; account-change handling then clears the single notification and refreshes provider registrations/watchers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the authentication provider through defaultAccountService.signIn with repo scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sign-in invocation per user activation of the notification choice; notification creation itself does not invoke sign-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This link-presentation flow did not offer or invoke sign-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial failed-link critical path and only blocks the user-triggered sign-in action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authentication-provider sign-in may perform provider/network work, followed by existing GitHub credential/resource refreshes after account change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: User-triggered once per choice activation; the live prompt is coalesced and provider entries are refreshed once per default-account change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recovery boundary was reachable from this notification because the notification did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to recover authenticated link details; it is not eagerly started for every failed link.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user action and the number of currently active distinct link entries refreshed after the account changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A MutableDisposable allows only one live authentication notification. Default-account change performs one registration refresh; data-channel entry and GitHub request sharing continue to coalesce duplicate resources.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account change intentionally invalidates/rebuilds provider watchers; existing data-channel and GitHub caches then govern warm presentation/resource reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in notification coalescing, explicit user gating, and account-change refresh behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of active links at sign-in varies, but refresh is a one-time recovery action rather than repeated eager work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the new expensive boundary is user initiated, bounded, and necessary for recovery.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and traced rich-link rendering, authentication, transport, rejected watcher, and sign-in scenarios. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
